bifrost: springboard/core/src/gamepad.rs, ff_effect.rs, ff_device.rs, force_effect.rs, rumble.rs, ff_escape.rs, haptic_request.rs (pure models; no evdev or shell wiring)
summary: Apple's Force Feedback framework is a legacy C API (FFCreateDevice, FFEffectDownload, FFEffectStart) for HID force-feedback devices such as wheels and joysticks. BifrOSt has pure models for the device capability bits, effects, device properties, haptic pulses and escape frames in springboard/core, but none is wired to an evdev node or the shell: the evdev reader does not upload effects, and the SDK's haptic() call is still dropped by the shell. Cooperative levels and polar or Cartesian directions are modelled in springboard/core/src/ff_cooperation.rs, but no input node uses them yet, and the driver plug-in interface is not exposed.

features.note: verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 7 tests. Wave 2 (theme-27, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. evdev bitmaps are parsed for keys, abs and switches only; no check for the FF capability bit, so a wheel or gamepad with force feedback is not identified as one

features.apple: FFDeviceCreateEffect, FFEffectDownload, FFEffectStart, FFEffectStop, FFEffectUnload, FFEffectSetParameters, FFEffectGetParameters, FFEFFECT, FFPERIODIC, FFCONSTANTFORCE, FFRAMPFORCE, FFCONDITION, FFCUSTOMFORCE, FFENVELOPE
features.note: verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 16 tests. Wave 5 (theme-05, parity/integration 93f283b0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. no EVIOCSFF upload, no FF effect structures, no EV_FF play events

features.apple: FFDeviceGetForceFeedbackProperty, FFDeviceSetForceFeedbackProperty, FFDeviceGetForceFeedbackState, FFDeviceSendForceFeedbackCommand, FFState, FFProperty
features.note: verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 16 tests. Wave 5 (theme-05, parity/integration 93f283b0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. no gain, autocenter or actuator-enable control

Frame model: a BifrOSt framing of the command code and payload with a 4096-byte payload limit, which encodes, decodes and splits several frames from one reply buffer (headless tests in springboard/core/tests/parity_sdk-complete-36.rs). Gap: no driver accepts the frame yet, so no escape reaches a device, and it is not verified on Midget.

Cooperative levels (shared or exclusive, foreground or background), one exclusive holder per device, and polar and Cartesian directions are tested headless in springboard/core/tests/parity_sdk-rest-16.rs. Gap: no input grab or effect upload uses the arbiter yet, and three-axis (spherical) directions are not modelled.

features.apple: ForceFeedback.h public interfaces, kFFAPI version variables, FFDeviceObjectReference, FFEffectObjectReference
features.note: Apple's plug-in model sits on IOKit/HID Manager, a macOS driver stack. On Linux the kernel evdev layer provides the equivalent, and BifrOSt does not expose it to apps, so the row is only a gap if app-facing FF is wanted

features.apple: No direct Force Feedback counterpart; closest is a generic haptic call
features.bifrost: springboard/core/src/haptic_request.rs (Requests, Outcome, MIN_INTERVAL_MS); springboard/core/src/force_effect.rs (Device::pulse); springboard/sdk/src/runtime.rs:273 (haptic() sends ToShell::Haptic); springboard/src/shell/apphost.rs:1184 (default arm drops it)
features.note: built on parity/team-k-force-feedback; not yet verified on Midget. Per-app policy (30 ms minimum between pulses, device slot check) is in core. The shell still has no ToShell::Haptic arm, so an app's haptic call does not reach a device Refreshed 2026-10-17: the evdev effect path exists in springboard/src/bare/pad_rumble.rs (Motor::open, play, stop; EVIOCSFF upload and EV_FF play events; tests pad_rumble::tests, declared in bare/mod.rs), with no caller yet.
a Settings switch only shown when a sysfs vibrator node exists; it does not drive any force-feedback device or effect

gaps: No effect reaches a controller yet: springboard/src/bare/pad_rumble.rs uploads effects (EVIOCSFF) and sends EV_FF play events (tests pad_rumble::tests), but nothing calls it, and springboard/src/bare/input.rs does not read EV_FF. Not verified on Midget
Device-level FF discovery is only a pure check (springboard/core/src/gamepad.rs supports_rumble, force_effect.rs supports_constant_force); the evdev node scan does not yet call it.
No SDK API for effects (constant, periodic, ramp, spring and friction) or for gain and autocenter properties.
The SDK haptic() call is dropped by the shell (springboard/src/shell/apphost.rs:1184 default arm); the per-app policy in springboard/core/src/haptic_request.rs has no caller yet.
Escape frames (springboard/core/src/ff_escape.rs) have no driver to write to; hardware escape commands stay unreachable until a device path exists.

Web gamepad input is compiled into the browser engine (springboard/apps/browser/engine/Cargo.toml:13, feature gamepad). Whether vibration actuators reach a device was not verified, and this is not covered by this framework row.
The MCP uinput virtual keyboard (springboard/mcp/src/keys.rs:28) sets ff_effects_max in its setup struct for the agent keyboard only; it does not create or drive a force-feedback device.
